sections.h2: Why does a Savannah house get two tax bills?
sections.html:
Georgia law makes a Savannah owner pay both city and county tax, and the two are mailed separately. The City of Savannah Revenue Department bills the city levy. The Chatham County Tax Commissioner bills county and school board taxes, as the city's calculation page explains.

  • City Revenue Department: 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455, weekdays 8:15 to 5. Mail: P.O. Box 1228, Savannah, GA 31402.
  • Chatham County Board of Assessors, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., Suite 113, 912-652-7271, for value, exemptions and appeals.
  • County Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100.

The city does not value property. City Council picks the millage rate, and the county assessors pick the value it multiplies.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Savannah homes?
sections.html:
Savannah's 106.85 land square miles held 147,780 people in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate in QuickFacts is 149,440, or 1,383 per square mile. The city has 58,192 households.

Renters outnumber owners: only 45.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. A middle-priced owned home is worth $248,900 and a middle rent is $1,382. Household income at the midpoint is $57,137, workers commute 20.7 minutes, and 7.6 percent of residents were born abroad. About 33.3 percent of adults hold at least a bachelor's degree.

Landlords and investors therefore shape resale demand next to owner-occupants. Rental parcels pay tax without homestead relief, which makes their bills higher for the same value.

In July 2026 the city proposed 11.749 mills for 2026, equal to 2025 and what it calls its lowest rate since 1987. The rollback rate, the one that would collect the same revenue as the year before, was 11.402.

County, school board and other rates stack on top. The city says parcels covered by Stephens-Day are shielded from the extra bite that keeping the rate would otherwise pass along as values rise.

sections.h2: When do Savannah's installments come due?
sections.html:
The city splits real property into two bills. April brings the first, typically due in mid-June and equal to half of last year's tax. September brings the second, typically due mid-November, repriced for current value, exemptions and rate. The city warns that dates are fixed when bills print and can shift.

The county's brochure, revised August 14, 2026, sets county real property at a first bill mailed by April 1 and due June 1, with the second mailed by September 15 and due November 15. Personal property tax is due by November 15 each year.

Funds must be received and posted by the due date. Partial payments are taken until the second due date, but the city sets up no payment plans. A bill that never arrived is still owed, and a copy is available online or at the Revenue Department.

sections.h2: What do late Savannah bills cost?
sections.html:
Interest runs at the prime rate plus 3 percent annually, accruing monthly, under O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 through 48-2-44. At 120 days overdue a 5 percent penalty attaches, with exceptions for small homestead balances, and recurs every 120 days to a cap of 20 percent.

An unpaid account can become a fi. fa., a lien that dents credit and can end in a tax sale. About six sales happen each year, each advertised four weeks ahead. The original owner may redeem for a year and a day by paying the winner the bid plus 20 percent.

During an appeal the city bills the lower of last year's value or 85 percent of the new value, due on the second installment date, then issues a corrected bill or refund.

sections.h2: How do Stephens-Day and homestead exemptions work in Chatham County?
sections.html:
You must own, occupy and claim the house as your legal residence on January 1. Applications are open year-round, but the assessors must receive yours within 45 days of the annual assessment notice for it to count that year. A Georgia license or ID and a vehicle registration at the same address are required, and a utility bill or voter card may be requested.

  • Standard homestead: $12,000 off county assessed value and $2,000 off school and state.
  • Stephens-Day, in place since 1999, and the statewide floating exemption both freeze a base year value. The owner gets whichever saves more.
  • Chatham senior exemption: age 65, net income of $10,000 or under, $30,000 off county and school assessed value.

Sales, deed changes and significant improvements move the base. A bedroom addition raises the base by its added value, and a demolition lowers it by the value lost. Opting in or out of HB 581 leaves existing base years alone. Solid waste and street light fees still apply.

sections.h2: Does a short-term rental change my homestead position in Savannah?
sections.html:
Savannah's vacation rental ordinance treats a property as owner-occupied only when the owner lives in the main unit as a primary residence. The applicant proves it with a valid homestead exemption, or else with a sworn affidavit and two forms of residency proof.

The link runs both ways. A homestead exemption on a house that is really an investment rental invites trouble at sale, so confirm your exemption status with the assessors before you list.

sections.h2: How can a Savannah owner appeal a Chatham County value?
sections.html:
Start with a written appeal to the Chatham County Board of Assessors within 45 days of the notice. The state's uniform appeal form is used, and the filing must say which of three methods you pick. Grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption.

  • Board of Equalization, with a later petition to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, which requires a certified appraisal submitted within the same 45 days. The assessors may accept or reject it, and review in Superior Court remains open.
  • Hearing officer, limited to non-homestead real property worth at least $500,000, or certain wireless property above $200,000 in total value, for disputes about value or uniformity.

The brochure also notes that a surviving spouse or minor child can petition Probate Court for a year's support within two years of a death, which can relieve property tax for the year named in the petition.

sections.h2: Where do I pay or ask questions in Chatham County?
sections.html:
County bills can be paid online at tax.chathamcountyga.gov by card or eCheck, with eChecks free and card fees applying. Mail goes to P.O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412. In person, offices on W. Oglethorpe Ave., Police Memorial Drive and Eisenhower Drive are open 8:30 to 5 on weekdays, and satellite offices on Wilmington Island Road, US 80 and Georgia Highway 21 work by appointment only.

The county office also bills Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. A returned check costs 5 percent of the amount with a $30 minimum. Tangible personal property other than vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value is $20,000 or less.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Savannah house that owes tax?
sections.html:
Yes. After the Revenue Department and the Tax Commissioner supply payoff figures, the title company clears both from your proceeds. A recorded lien shows up in the title search well before the closing date.

Cash offers avoid lender appraisals and repair lists. Compare each against a normal listing less repairs, back tax and holding costs.

faqs.q: Which office collects Savannah city property tax?
faqs.a: The City of Savannah Revenue Department, at 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455. County and school taxes are collected separately by the Chatham County Tax Commissioner.

faqs.q: When does Savannah's second property tax bill come due?
faqs.a: Typically in mid-November. The county brochure puts county bills at November 15, while the city sets its own date when bills print.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window in Chatham County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the annual notice of assessment, with the first filing going to the Chatham County Board of Assessors.

faqs.q: What happens to a Savannah bill that is 120 days late?
faqs.a: A 5 percent penalty is added, on top of monthly interest at prime plus 3 percent a year. It recurs every 120 days up to 20 percent.

faqs.q: What does Stephens-Day do for a Chatham County owner?
faqs.a: It is a county homestead exemption, active since 1999, that holds taxable value at a base year amount plus improvements. Where the statewide floating exemption would save more, the owner gets that one instead.
